newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks seen firmer on stable yen, Dow's rise.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks seen firmer on stable yen, Dow's rise.

text.p: Tokyo stocks are likely to gain ground on Monday, supported by a stable currency market and a record rally in Dow industrials on Friday, brokers said.

Expectations of a new inflow of money from domestic pension funds this week should also lend a support to the market, they said. But any rise could be slow, as export-orientated issues which led a broad rally in recent months have been losing momentum.
On Friday, the 225-share Nikkei average finished down 36.11 points, or 0.18 percent, at 20,528.35. Its September futures ended flat at 20,590.

"As long as the dollar trades between 113 and 116 yen, the yen's stability will help the stock market and the Nikkei 225 should test the 21,000 level this week," said Yasuo Ueki, general manager at Nikko Securities Co Ltd.
But he said any rise above 20,600 would be slow due to profit taking. The index was likely to range from 20,400 to 20,800 on Monday, he added.
On Friday, the Dow industrials ended up 70.57 points at 7,782.04. It was the sixth consecutive record closing high in the blue chip index.
